status_summary: EO 14154 (2025-01-20) revoked the order that authorized CEQ's NEPA regulations and directed CEQ to propose rescinding them. CEQ removed its regulations (40 CFR parts 1500-1508) by an interim final rule effective 2025-04-11 and a final rule effective 2026-01-08, concluding NEPA gives it an advisory role rather than authority to bind agencies. Agencies now rely on their own NEPA procedures, and CEQ has issued non-binding guidance, a template for agency procedures (2025-09-29) and categorical-exclusion guidance (2026-04-09). This pursues the Mandate's streamlining goal by removal, not by rewriting the 2020 rule as recommended. Court deference to agency NEPA conclusions rests on a 2025 Supreme Court decision CEQ cites.

timeline.event: CEQ publishes an interim final rule removing its NEPA implementing regulations; a CEQ notice later gives the effective date as 2025-04-11.
CEQ publishes a notice withdrawing its NEPA guidance on greenhouse gas emissions and climate change.
CEQ issues updated guidance with a template for agency NEPA procedures developed with a federal working group (published 2025-10-02); the guidance is not binding.

CEQ's final rule adopts the interim rule without change and removes all versions of its NEPA regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations; CEQ cites the Supreme Court's 2025 NEPA decision on deference.
CEQ issues guidance on establishing and using categorical exclusions, replacing its 2010 guidance (published 2026-04-13); the guidance is not binding.

Per a Harvard Environmental and Energy Law Program tracker, CEQ withdraws 18 older guidance memos as obsolete or misaligned with current policy; the tracker lists no lawsuit challenging the removal of CEQ's NEPA regulations.

title: Rewrite CEQ's NEPA regulations to streamline review and limit judicial review
